gen_risks.description: Increased frequency and severity of climate hazards, flash floods, and storms disrupting project service delivery and activity implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate-resilient engineering standards for training center facilities, maintain flexible project workplans, and utilize CERC activation if major climate shocks occur.
gen_risks.evidence: increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and climate shocks may cause disruptions in service delivery

gen_risks.description: Unreliable electricity grid and flood hazards disrupting the continuous operation of the digital labor market system and Employability Portal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure backup power generators, implement automated offline backup protocols, and host the Employment Observatory on a secure cloud-based platform.
gen_risks.evidence: intense rainfall and floods which may disrupt electricity access

gen_risks.description: Delays in financial reporting, transaction recording, and disbursement of sub-grants/stipends to beneficiaries due to complex fiduciary processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated financial accountant, customize the computerized accounting software, update POM FM guidelines, and contract a professional Payment Service Provider.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in availing funds for beneficiaries resulting from possible non-compliance in selection criteria

gen_risks.description: Inter-institutional coordination bottlenecks between MLSSS, AFAP, and sectoral line ministries causing delays in workplan approvals and technical specifications.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a unified PIU combining SPRRP and project staff, operationalize a Ministerial Coordination Committee, and define detailed operational workflows in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in preparing annual workplans and implementing interventions due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders

gen_risks.description: Risk of elite capture and exclusion of vulnerable youth, women, and remote populations during beneficiary selection for grants, scholarships, and internships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize objective socio-economic targeting criteria based on the Unique Social Registry (USR), enforce a minimum 50% female participation quota, and conduct targeted outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of elite capture in the selection of beneficiaries

gen_risks.description: Exposure of young female beneficiaries to sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) during vocational training or internship placements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a dedicated GBV/SEA/SH Social Specialist at AFAP, mandate SEA/SH prevention mechanisms in training agreements, and implement a responsive Grievance Redress Mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: risks of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH), particularly for young women

gen_risks.description: Public TVET institutions failing to deliver market-relevant training due to outdated equipment, infrastructure gaps, and instructor shortages.
gen_risks.mitigation: Form Workforce Development Committees with private employers, fund instructor upskilling, and procure modern training equipment through performance-based institutional agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps

gen_risks.description: Generation of construction debris and operational waste from sub-grant recipient micro-enterprises causing localized pollution in fragile island ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply ESF environmental screening to all sub-projects, enforce proper waste disposal practices during rehabilitation works, and provide environmental management training to MSMEs.
gen_risks.evidence: generation of solid waste, obsolete equipment, and minor construction debris

gen_risks.description: Schedule delays in designing, procuring, and constructing the new multi-use technical training center on the isolated island of Príncipe.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure preliminary studies and architectural design consultancies early, utilize market-informed island cost estimates, and maintain close procurement oversight via AFAP.
gen_risks.evidence: structural constraints specific to Príncipe—including geographic isolation and a severely limited pool of skilled workers

gen_risks.description: Unstructured youth emigration leading to brain drain or precarious, low-wage employment abroad without formal skill recognition.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured labor mobility orientation, align TVET training with destination country skill shortages, and mobilize technical assistance for Global Skill Partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: many Santomean migrants end up in precarious jobs with low wages, often below their skill level

gen_risks.description: Limited absorption capacity and slow growth within the small domestic formal private sector constraining long-term graduate employment and MSME expansion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide comprehensive MSME incubation and grant packages to expand enterprise hiring capacity, while offering structured self-employment and labor mobility pathways.
gen_risks.evidence: STP’s small-island context, where the entrepreneurial ecosystem is nascent and scalable innovation is limited

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic volatility and import cost inflation eroding project procurement purchasing power and reducing real values of startup grants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct regular financial plan reviews, manage budget allocations flexibly through the project procurement plan, and provide financial management training to grant recipients.
gen_risks.evidence: geopolitical turmoil (which drove volatility in fuel and food import costs), recurrent flooding, and an electricity crisis

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
